candidate_concepts.label: Bayes Theorem (Bayes Rule)
candidate_concepts.description: Bayes theorem relates conditional probabilities: P(B|A) = P(A|B) * P(B) / P(A). It allows updating probabilities based on new evidence.

candidate_concepts.label: Naive Bayes Classifier
candidate_concepts.description: A probabilistic machine learning algorithm that applies Bayes theorem with the 'naive' assumption that features are independent given the class. It computes the posterior probability for each class and predicts the one with the maximum.
coverage_criteria: State the naive assumption.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source defines and explains the Naive Bayes algorithm in the section 'What is Naive Bayes Algorithm?' and 'How Naive Bayes Works?' with a golf example.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is the central concept, broken down into its two key parts (Bayes theorem + independence) which can be covered in a few focused questions.

candidate_concepts.label: Feature Independence Assumption (Why 'Naive')
candidate_concepts.description: Naive Bayes assumes all features are independent of each other given the class label. This unrealistic assumption is why it is called 'naive', but it often still works well in practice.
